newsitem.title: CANADA: Judge dismisses Oppenheimer & Co UGG suit.
newsitem.headline: Judge dismisses Oppenheimer & Co UGG suit.

text.p: A Manitoba judge on Friday dismissed a suit by a New York arbitrager aimed at forcing an early shareholder vote on issues tied to an equity deal between United Grain Growers Ltd and Archer Daniels Midland Co.
"I dismiss the application. No improper purpose was proven for postponing the meeting to July 17," Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench Justice Freda Steel told the court.

Oppenheimer & Co filed the lawsuit in Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench last week to force UGG to hold a vote June 26 on new share issuance and a poison pill instead of at a July 17 meeting. The vote would put a seal of approval on a deal with Archer Daniels Midland Co.
On May 29 UGG announced the tentative deal with ADM that would see C$113 million change hands and ADM acquire a 45 percent stake in the grain handler at C$16 a share.
Oppenheimer owns 13.16 percent of UGG's outstanding limited common voting shares while a joint company of Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators owns 14.98 percent.
AWP and MPE scuttled a C$13.75 per share hostile takeover bid for UGG in March after Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench ruled UGG's poison pill plan was legally valid.
